summary: In prison, Joseph helped Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker understand their dreams, giving the credit to God. The cupbearer was set free but forgot all about Joseph.

story_reel.narration: While Joseph was in prison, two of Pharaoh's officials were thrown in too: the cupbearer, who served Pharaoh his drinks, and the baker, who made Pharaoh's bread. One morning, Joseph noticed they both looked sad. 'Why are you so sad today?' he asked. 'We each had a dream, and no one can tell us what it means.' Joseph said, 'Don't interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.' The cupbearer dreamed of a vine with three branches that grew grapes, which he squeezed into Pharaoh's cup. Joseph said, 'In three days, Pharaoh will give you your job back.' Then Joseph asked, 'When you're free, please remember me and tell Pharaoh about me.' The baker's dream was different. He carried three baskets of bread on his head, but birds ate from them. Sadly, his dream meant his story would not end well. Three days later, everything happened just as Joseph said. The cupbearer got his job back. But he forgot all about Joseph. Two whole years went by. Joseph had to keep waiting and trusting God.

identity_focus.core_truth: I can use the gifts Yahweh gives me to help others and give Him the credit.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: Joseph noticed when others were sad and helped them. Who around you might need someone to notice them?

quiz.question: What did Joseph say about understanding dreams?
quiz.explanation: Joseph said, 'Don't interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.'

quiz.question: What did Joseph say would happen to the cupbearer in three days?
options: He would get his job back
quiz.explanation: Joseph said, 'Within three more days, Pharaoh will restore you to your office.'

quiz.question: What did the cupbearer do when he got out of prison?
quiz.explanation: The chief cupbearer didn't remember Joseph, but forgot him.

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You for the gifts You've given me. Help me notice when others are sad, use my gifts to help them, and always give You the credit. Amen.

companion.message: Those two years felt so long. I wondered if anyone would ever remember me. But God hadn't forgotten. He was setting up something bigger than I could imagine.

review.notes: The baker's execution (Genesis 40:19, 22) is softened to 'his story would not end well.' Confirm this is acceptable.
